payload.instruction: Move the mug to the right of the headphones

decision.question: Does comparison of the source and edited images establish that the source mug itself has been moved to the right of the headphones?
decision.criteria: Pass only when the combined visual evidence establishes both correspondence to the source mug and its position to the right of the edited headphones. Compare both edited mug candidates using body proportions, rim and interior, handle geometry, relative scale and appearance, accounting for changes in framing and possible rotation. Generic mug shape, similar taper or presence on the right is insufficient when those cues do not distinguish the right-hand candidate from the left-hand candidate. Consider evidence supporting and contradicting each correspondence; do not dismiss differences in interior, handle or appearance without weighing them together with the supporting cues. Exact color, scale and handle orientation preservation are not separate requirements. Fail when the evidence establishes that the source mug remains left of the headphones or otherwise has not reached the requested right-side position. Use unknown when the source mug's correspondence or resulting position remains unresolved. A blurred patch alone establishes neither retained identity nor successful removal, and lack of proof of completion is not proof of failure.
decision.binding: Target: the light-blue mug with a left-facing handle in the source image. Reference: the headphones in each image. Compare the source mug with both edited candidates: the pale mug left of the headphones and the dark-interior mug right of the headphones. Inspect the far-left blue blurred patch only as ambiguous possible residual evidence, not as an identified mug. Assess whether the full cue combination distinguishes the right-hand candidate as the relocated source mug rather than a separate mug; if neither candidate can be identified reliably, return unknown. Compare object-relative placement with the edited headphones, allowing for changed framing, scale and headphone arrangement rather than relying on raw pixel coordinates.
